items.text: This sunny corridor, tucked away from the bustle of the office, now serves as a classroom where Vila holds classes for the children.
Art, physical education, and the Foundation's general education courses.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Alright, children.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Please repeat the rules one by one, starting with our comrades at the front.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Comrade Pyotr?

items.speaker: Pyotr
items.text: First, no running, no horseplay!

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Second, don't climb out of the window.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: A rule made very specially for you, Comrade Pasono.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Next, Comrade Nina.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Third, always raise your hand to ask questions.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Exactly. Comrade Avgust?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Do not wander away without your comrades.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Don't look for Vila on your own.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: That's right, Comrade Avgust. Going out all alone is dangerous, even in a safe place, like the Foundation.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: There is no place that is perfectly safe, and no place stays safe forever.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Besides, I'll always be right here with you, so why would you be looking for me?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Did you stop writing, Vila?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Mr. Raccoon isn't here today.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Mr. Name Day has his own work to do, so do we.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: And our work today is to play chess, fold sea swallows, read books, and explore our own interests.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Dismissed!
Like a rocket, at her word, the kids launch upwards, bouncing against the walls, until only two remain.
Avgust stands beside Nina, looking at her. The little girl wears a worried face. Vila brings herself to them.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What's wrong, Nina?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Ms. Vila ...

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: When are we going back to Rayashki?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: I asked Mr. Name Day the same question, and he said "soon." But how soon is soon?

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: "Soon" means tomorrow.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Mom always said "soon," "it won't be long," "everything will be fine when you wake up tomorrow."

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: So, I think they have the same meaning.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: But it's already tomorrow. It's been a lot of tomorrows, and we're still here.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: I don't understand. And I miss mama.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I think "soon" means that we will go home. That is for certain. And we could be on our way there at any moment.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: But, when will that be?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I'm sorry, Nina. I shouldn't have said that.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Honesty is important, so honestly, I don't know.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But I am sure that we will return home once it is safe. Mr. Name Day has been helping us with just that.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Though he shouldn't have to do these for us.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Mr. Raccoon keeps going in and out.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: He left through the front hall, but he brings fewer things back every time.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Ms. Vila!

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Avgust always says it's a sea swallow, but I say this is a paper plane.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: It's not as powerful as a real fighter jet, but I made it with our last piece of paper.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Rare things are always more valuable, like canned meat and sausages.
Suddenly, the paper plane in Vila's hand becomes heavier than a real jet.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: I'm sure you will be able to take us home with this.
Is it folded paper or military-grade steel? She can't tell.
And nothing seems to fit as an answer.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Thank you, Pasono.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: This is indeed a well-made plane.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: This is a sea swallow, an "eternal soul"! It will fly far, far enough to reach the town.

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: Can it take us all back too?

items.speaker: Nina
items.text: I miss everyone. I miss Rayashki.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We will go home.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Yay! I've practiced my paper folding. So I can make real good stuff now!

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: I want to make one for Uncle Knut too.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: But we're running out of the paper Mr. Name Day brought us.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Vila, Pasono says we're running out of "eternal souls."

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Could we give him other things that are like an "eternal soul"?  Something he can fold into more sea swallows and other things.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Okay. I'll see what I can do.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: Why do you call paper "eternal souls"? Souls are for people, not paper!

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: I once read a story about a Rusalka princess to my sister. The princess traded her fish tail and her voice for a pair of legs, but she didn't get what she wanted and turned into foam.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: I don't like that story. That princess is like Ivan the Fool. She doesn't make sense.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Vila is not Ivan the Fool.

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: I'm not referring to Ms. Vila! She's not a princess. Besides, the book says Rusalki will eventually turn into foam because they don't have an "eternal soul."

items.speaker: Pasono
items.text: That's not Ms. Vila's case. She must have one.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: No, paper is the name we give souls, Vila told me ...
Amused by their discussion, Vila decides it best not to intervene.
Pyotr, though, is anxious. As the oldest boy, he feels he must break up any fights, to keep everyone in line. Vila gently taps him on the shoulder to reassure him.
The sound of the telegraph and typewriter harmonizes, echoing in this little room.
Wearing headphones, Name Day is listening to the telegram and transcribing it through the typewriter.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: "I wish to hold your hand tightly."

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Why is it in reversed order?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: "Your most loyal yet worst friend,"

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: "Windsong."

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Hmm?
Familiar footsteps approach, followed by a knock.
Name Day concentrates fully on the incoming telegram, having no idea of the coming intrusion.
Mr. Name Day, are you in there?
Hmm. This should be the place.
Mr. Name Day, are you in there?
Hmm. This should be the place.
This is where he stores all his "collections."
That sound. Is that a typewriter?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Shoot!

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: It's Ms. Vila!!
He silently screams, realizing it's too late to hide either the letter or the telegraph.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: No, she must not see—

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Mr. Name Day? I heard your voice. Sorry to bother you now, but I really need to know ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: When can we ...
"It won't be the town you remembered or the utopia we tried to build."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Go back to Rayashki?
